title: Logarithmic derivative ideals under one test transformation
statement:
Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a closed immersion of smooth finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes and let $B$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary transverse to $N$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here the boundary condition means that etale locally $N$ is a coordinate subspace and each boundary component is a coordinate hyperplane, with distinct boundary parameters independent of the support equations [def-weil-etale-morphism]. A smooth center has normal crossings with this boundary when it too is a coordinate subspace in such coordinates; it may be contained in boundary components. Let $J\subseteq\mathcal O_N$ be a coherent ideal and $b\ge1$ [pqf-def-coherent]. Define $D_B^jJ$ as the ideal generated by iterated $\mathbf Q$-derivatives of sections of $J$ of lengths at most $j$, using derivations preserving each boundary ideal on $N$. These are coherent ideals. If $J_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q$, then $(D_B^jJ)_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^{q-j}$ for $0\le j\le q$.

Let $\sigma:Z'\to Z$ be one of the following: an open restriction; the projection $Z\times\mathbf A^1\to Z$, adjoining its zero section to the boundary; a blowup with smooth center $T\subset N$ on which $J_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^b$, having normal crossings with $B$; or a blowup of the intersection of two distinct boundary components [def-nagata-global-blowup]. In the cosupport-center case take $N'$ to be the strict transform, let $e$ be a local exceptional equation and put $J'=e^{-b}\sigma^*J$; in the other cases use ordinary pullback of $N,J$. For a boundary-intersection blowup, strict transform and inverse image of $N$ agree. Let $B'$ be the ordered strict-transform boundary with the new exceptional component appended, when there is one [def-nagata-strict-transform]. For each $0\le j<b$, the same operation is allowed for $(D_B^jJ,b-j)$, its transform $J_j'$ is regular, and
$$J_j'\subseteq D_{B'}^j(J').$$
Here $J_j'=e^{-(b-j)}\sigma^*(D_B^jJ)$ for a cosupport-center blowup and $J_j'=\sigma^*(D_B^jJ)$ otherwise. An operation that is both kinds of blowup uses the indicated chosen transform rule, not both rules at once. Empty strict transforms are allowed.

For any smooth morphism $g:Y\to Z$ of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, put $N_Y=Y\times_ZN$ and let $B_Y$ be the pulled-back boundary (locally splitting disconnected components if needed, without changing their ideals). Then
$$D_{B_Y}^j(J\mathcal O_{N_Y})=(D_B^jJ)\mathcal O_{N_Y}.$$
This equality uses all $\mathbf Q$-derivations, including relative derivations, and holds for every $j\ge0$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution input only); detailed proof source absent locally: Bierstone--Milman, Functoriality in Resolution of Singularities, Publ. RIMS 44 (2008), §§3.1--3.2, Lemmas 3.2--3.3 and Corollary 3.4, pp.620--622. Read online at https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043; no Stacks tag states this logarithmic marked transform lemma.

proof.text: Work locally on $N$ in the etale coordinates supplied by the boundary hypothesis, writing $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, with boundary ideals $(x_a)$ for $a\in H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The affine etale criterion gives $H_1(L)=0$ and $\Omega_{\mathrm{relative}}=0$; the formally-etale differential base-change isomorphism then identifies $\Omega_{N/\mathbf Q}$ with the free module with basis $dx_a$. By the universal property of differentials, every derivation is uniquely $\sum_a c_a\partial_{x_a}$. It preserves each $(x_a)$, $a\in H$, exactly when $c_a\in(x_a)$ for these indices. Thus the logarithmic derivations are generated by $L_a=x_a\partial_{x_a}$ for $a\in H$ and $L_a=\partial_{x_a}$ otherwise. This also applies to any of the smooth etale coordinate charts used below. The coordinate maps here can be chosen on open neighbourhoods: start with a smooth chart from the local normal-form theorem; the differential isomorphism just used gives a basis. The local boundary equations have independent differentials by the stated normal crossings condition. Complete these with some smooth-chart coordinate differentials and apply the etale-at-point criterion, which itself supplies an open neighbourhood on which this chosen coordinate map is etale. Thus the coherence argument below uses an open cover, rather than an unproved descent assertion. No claim about transforming derivative ideals has been used.

source.place: Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, final assertion; polynomial differentials by their universal property

proof.text: Choose finitely many generators $f_\nu$ of $J$ locally. Leibniz gives $L(af)=L(a)f+aL(f)$, so $D_B^jJ$ is generated by the finitely many words $L_{a_s}\cdots L_{a_1}f_\nu$, $0\le s\le j$. Induct on $j$: differentiating a coefficient times an old word adds either an old word or one word of length one more. These ideals localize correctly, since $L(a/s)=L(a)/s-aL(s)/s^2$; conversely old words remain available after restriction. Hence they define quasi-coherent ideals of finite type. Since a field is Noetherian and $N$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma applies. The coherent/finite-type criterion now proves coherence for every $j$, including $J=0$.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; finite word argument written here

proof.text: For any derivation of a local ring, the product rule sends $\mathfrak m^q$ into $\mathfrak m^{q-1}$ for $q\ge1$: write an element as a sum of coefficients times products of $q$ elements of $\mathfrak m$ and differentiate. The term differentiating the coefficient still lies in $\mathfrak m^q$, and every other term contains $q-1$ factors in $\mathfrak m$. Iteration proves $(D_B^jJ)_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^{q-j}$ for $j\le q$ whenever $J_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q$. This works at nonclosed points, for $q=0$, and for the zero ideal. In particular every given cosupport center is also in the cosupport of $(D_B^jJ,b-j)$ for $j<b$.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, resolution context only; agent calculation following Bierstone--Milman 2008, §§3.1--3.2, pp.620--622, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043 (read online; PDF absent locally); elementary Leibniz estimate

proof.text: Consider the cosupport-center blowup. Apply the marked controlled-blowup chart statement first to $(J,b)$ and then, using Steps 2--3, to $(D_B^jJ,b-j)$ for every $j<b$. The same smooth center and the same boundary satisfy its hypotheses, and $b-j\ge1$. For each application its ideal-power conclusion gives $A\subseteq\mathcal I_{T,N}^{c}$, where $(A,c)$ is the marked ideal in question. This justifies division by $e^c$ on every chart. It gives regular coherent transforms, $N'\cong\operatorname{Bl}_T N$, smoothness and the new normal crossings boundary. On each surviving chart choose the center ideal $(x_s:s\in S)$ and a pivot $i\in S$; write $e=x_i$, $y_s=x_s/e$ for $s\in S\setminus\{i\}$, and leave other coordinates unchanged. The new boundary has $e=0$, $y_s=0$ for $s\in(H\cap S)\setminus\{i\}$, and $x_a=0$ for $a\in H\setminus S$. Components contained in the center disappear, exactly as allowed in that statement. Outside the center the assertion reduces to restriction.

source.place: Tags 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, and 0FUT, lemma-blowup; divisors.tex Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; existing marked smooth-flag chart statement

proof.text: On this chart, each old logarithmic generator $L_a$ admits a regular logarithmic derivation $V_a$ satisfying $V_a(\sigma^*F)=e\sigma^*(L_aF)$. For $a\notin S$, take $V_a=eL_a$ on the unchanged coordinate. For $a\in S\setminus\{i\}$, take $V_a=\partial_{y_a}$ if $a\notin H$, and $V_a=e y_a\partial_{y_a}$ if $a\in H$. In the first case $y_a=0$ is not a boundary component; in the second it is, and its ideal is preserved. Substituting $\sigma^*x_i=e$, $\sigma^*x_s=ey_s$ checks the displayed identity on every old coordinate. By the differential-coordinate description in Step 1, it is then an identity of derivations on regular functions, not only on polynomials.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, resolution context only; agent calculation following Bierstone--Milman 2008, §§3.1--3.2, pp.620--622, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043 (read online; PDF absent locally); nonpivot cases of Lemma 3.1 expanded

proof.text: For the pivot put $W=e\partial_e-\sum_{s\in S\setminus\{i\}}y_s\partial_{y_s}$. If $i\notin H$, take $V_i=W$; if $i\in H$, take $V_i=eW$. Evaluation on $x_i=e$ and $x_s=ey_s$ proves the identity of Step 5 in both cases. Every term of $W$ preserves each new boundary ideal, so $V_i$ does too. All $V_a$ therefore preserve $(e)$, and $\lambda_a=V_a(e)/e$ is regular: it is $0$ for $a\ne i$, $1$ for an ordinary pivot, and $e$ for a boundary pivot. These formulas include centers contained in old boundary components and centers disjoint from them.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, resolution context only; agent calculation following Bierstone--Milman 2008, §§3.1--3.2, pp.620--622, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043 (read online; PDF absent locally); pivot cases of Lemma 3.1 expanded

proof.text:
Let $A$ be any of the derivative ideals in Step 4 with positive mark $c$, and take a generator $F$ with regular controlled transform $h=e^{-c}\sigma^*F$. Steps 5--6 and Leibniz give the exact regular identity
$$e^{-(c-1)}\sigma^*(L_aF)=e^{-c}V_a(e^ch)=V_a(h)+c\lambda_a h.$$
The transformed undifferentiated generator is $e^{-(c-1)}\sigma^*F=eh$. It follows directly from the finite-generator description in Step 2 that the mark-$(c-1)$ transform of $D_BA$ is contained in the ideal generated by the mark-$c$ transform of $A$ and its new logarithmic derivatives, whenever $c\ge2$. For a coefficient $u$, the additional term is explicit: $e^{-(c-1)}\sigma^*(L_a(uF))=e\sigma^*(L_a u)h+\sigma^*(u)(V_a(h)+c\lambda_a h)$. Both summands belong to that same ideal, so differentiating arbitrary sections adds no generators outside it.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, resolution context only; agent calculation following Bierstone--Milman 2008, §§3.1--3.2, pp.620--622, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043 (read online; PDF absent locally); Lemma 3.3, exceptional-factor calculation

proof.text: Set $A_j=D_B^jJ$ and $K_j=e^{-(b-j)}\sigma^*A_j$ for $0\le j<b$. The base case is $K_0=J'$. Suppose $j+1<b$ and $K_j\subseteq D_{B'}^jJ'$. Step 7 applies with $A=A_j$, $c=b-j\ge2$, and gives $K_{j+1}\subseteq D_{B'}(K_j)$. Differentiating an inclusion of ideals preserves inclusion; the word definition gives $D_{B'}(D_{B'}^jJ')=D_{B'}^{j+1}J'$. Thus $K_{j+1}\subseteq D_{B'}^{j+1}J'$, completing the induction. For $b=1$ only the base case occurs. An empty strict transform has the unique zero ideal sheaf and satisfies every assertion. This proves the claimed inclusion for the controlled transform rule.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, resolution context only; agent calculation following Bierstone--Milman 2008, §§3.1--3.2, pp.620--622, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043 (read online; PDF absent locally); Corollary 3.4, induction written explicitly

proof.text: Away from the boundary intersection the blowup is an isomorphism and Step 2 applies. Near that intersection, work with boundary coordinates $x_p,x_q$; on the $p$-chart put $e=x_p$ and $y=x_q/x_p$. Apply the marked-blowup chart statement to $Z\hookrightarrow Z$, center $V(x_p,x_q)$, and zero ideal with mark $1$. It gives the ambient smooth charts and boundary equations $e,y$ and the other old boundary coordinates; the $q$-chart is symmetric. The equations $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ of $N$ are unchanged because the boundary parameters are independent of them. Quotienting the chart presentation by $(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ gives precisely the intrinsic blowup chart on $N$ along $V(x_p,x_q)$. Apply the marked-blowup chart statement to the pair $N\hookrightarrow N$ and the zero ideal with mark $1$ to see that these quotient charts are smooth and $e$ is an exceptional coordinate. In particular $e$ is a non-zero-divisor in the quotient by $(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$. If $e^k f$ lies in that ideal, cancellation in the quotient gives $f=0$ there. Thus $(z_1,\ldots,z_r):e^\infty=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$. By the definition of scheme-theoretic strict transform this proves that the inverse image of $N$ equals its strict transform. It also proves the required smoothness and transversality. If the intersection misses $N$, its entire inverse image is outside the center, so the restriction case already proves the assertion.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, coordinate proof; and the explicit independent-support-equation calculation above

proof.text: Here old logarithmic generators lift without an exceptional multiplier: $x_p\partial_{x_p}$ lifts to $e\partial_e-y\partial_y$, $x_q\partial_{x_q}$ to $y\partial_y$, and every other $L_a$ is unchanged. Substitution checks $\widetilde L_a(\sigma^*F)=\sigma^*(L_aF)$; all these lifts preserve every new boundary ideal. A word of length at most $j$ in the old generators therefore pulls back to a word of length at most $j$ in logarithmic derivations of the new chart. Step 2 yields $\sigma^*(D_B^jJ)\subseteq D_{B'}^j(\sigma^*J)$. Both ideals are regular and coherent by the same finite-word construction, with no exceptional division. The operation is independent of cosupport and is allowed for every mark. If this blowup is also a cosupport-center blowup, Step 8 applies when its controlled rule is chosen, and the present argument applies when its ordinary-pullback rule is chosen; the two rules are never identified.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, resolution context only; agent calculation following Bierstone--Milman 2008, §§3.1--3.2, pp.620--622, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043 (read online; PDF absent locally); Lemma 3.3, exceptional-test-blowup case

proof.text: For smooth pullback, first use the local normal-form theorem to restrict to neighbourhoods with fixed smooth relative dimensions for $g$ and $N\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$. Apply smooth relative-dimension permanence on these neighbourhoods. It gives a smooth finite-type support $N_Y$ and a smooth map $h:N_Y\to N$. The etale local normal form of $h$ factors it locally as an etale map to $N\times\mathbf A^r$. Combining a boundary coordinate chart $(x_a)$ on $N$ with the relative coordinates $(t_\mu)$, the differential isomorphism of Step 1 gives all derivations upstairs as combinations of $\partial_{x_a}$ and $\partial_{t_\mu}$. Preserving each pulled-back boundary ideal makes the horizontal coefficients divisible by $x_a$ for $a\in H$. Thus all logarithmic derivations upstairs are generated by the horizontal lifts of the $L_a$ and the relative $\partial_{t_\mu}$. Splitting a disconnected boundary component locally does not change its principal ideal or this condition.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; Tags 01VB and 01VA, smooth base change and composition; algebra.tex Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega

proof.text:
For any ideal $A$ on $N$, every generator $h^*F$ of $A\mathcal O_{N_Y}$ is killed by a relative $\partial_{t_\mu}$, and its horizontal logarithmic derivatives are exactly $h^*(L_aF)$. For a general section $u h^*F$, Leibniz adds $(\delta u)h^*F$, already in the extended ideal. Consequently
$$D_{B_Y}(A\mathcal O_{N_Y})=(D_BA)\mathcal O_{N_Y}.$$
The inclusion from right to left uses the horizontal lifts; the reverse uses all upstairs logarithmic derivations, including the relative ones. Starting at $A=J$ and inducting on $j$ proves the equality for every $j\ge0$. These are local equalities of ideals, so they glue, without injectivity or surjectivity assumptions on the smooth map.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, resolution context only; agent calculation following Bierstone--Milman 2008, §§3.1--3.2, pp.620--622, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043 (read online; PDF absent locally); Lemma 3.2(4), explicit horizontal/relative calculation

proof.text: An open restriction preserves derivative ideals because the construction is local (Step 2). For the line projection with zero-section boundary, the logarithmic frame consists of the horizontal $L_a$ together with $t\partial_t$. The latter kills every pulled-back generator of $J$; the same Leibniz argument as in Step 12 gives $D_{B\cup\{t=0\}}^j(J\mathcal O_{N\times\mathbf A^1})=(D_B^jJ)\mathcal O_{N\times\mathbf A^1}$. Hence the desired ordinary-transform inclusion is an equality in these two cases, and regularity and admissibility hold. Together with Steps 3--10 this covers every test operation, each $0\le j<b$, every empty support, and all the clauses of the statement.
